title: U.S. House · Texas's 23rd District
area: West and South Texas, stretching from San Antonio's outskirts along the border to El Paso County.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Tony Gonzales trailed Brandon Herrera in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, 41.8% to 43.3%, forcing a runoff; Gonzales withdrew before the May 26, 2026 runoff, which was canceled, and Herrera advanced. Katy Padilla Stout won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary. Ben Mendoza, a perennial candidate who previously ran for El Paso mayor, is on the ballot as an independent.

candidates.name: Brandon Herrera
candidates.ballotNote: Led the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 43.3% of the vote, then advanced to the general election after incumbent Tony Gonzales withdrew and the scheduled runoff was canceled.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says he will fight for national concealed carry reciprocity and block red flag laws and new firearms restrictions.
positions.quote: fight for national concealed carry reciprocity and block any attempt to pass Red Flag laws or impose new firearms restrictions

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says he will sponsor legislation so education dollars follow the student to public, private or parochial schools.
positions.quote: ensuring education dollars follow the student, whether they attend public, private, or parochial school

positions.summary: Campaign issues page pledges to protect girls' and women's sports and opposes requiring female athletes to compete against transgender women.
positions.quote: ensure that America's daughters won't have their athletic careers stolen by woke leftists that force them to compete with men

candidates.researchNotes: No Candidate Connection survey on file; his campaign website was not readable in this session beyond confirming its existence.

candidates.name: Katy Padilla Stout
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.1% of the vote over three other candidates.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says she supports expanding Medicare to cover all Americans and, short of that, strengthening the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: I support expanding our Medicare system to cover all Americans.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says no constitutional right is without reasonable limits and names universal background checks, a bump stock ban and red-flag laws as measures most Americans support.
positions.quote: No constitutional right is without reasonable limits grounded in common sense, and laws concerning responsible gun ownership should be no exception.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says women's reproductive rights need to be protected and the government should not be involved in those decisions.
positions.quote: I believe women’s reproductive rights need to be protected.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says she supports raising the minimum wage.
positions.quote: we should invest in families and strengthen our workforce by raising the minimum wage and requiring paid parental leave
